scope: Consistency challenge of Batches 01–04 and independent challenge of Batches 05–07; source packets unchanged

findings.finding: Unknown counts are 82/240 in A and 3/151 in B. A leaves many general activity comparisons unknown; B commonly labels a stronger route as coordination and adds tactical/pawn/endgame tags. This is coder threshold variation, not measured behavioral variation.
findings.required_correction_or_limit: Do not compare category rates or interpret unknown disparity as a batch effect. Use a common category evidence rule. Retain unknowns unless exact context supports a category; do not fill A to match B.

findings.finding: A includes stable straddlers at any .04/.05/.06 threshold. B lists seven unresolved .05 cases, omitting at least these eight source-tagged subthreshold .04 straddlers.
findings.required_correction_or_limit: Use one separate sensitivity population across packets. Add these eight source-tagged cases to a harmonized sensitivity overlay; retain supported_subthreshold at .05 and do not add them to supported category counts. Reconcile old schema sensitivities from raw retained ranges rather than assuming identical field names.

findings.finding: The rationale describes Qb3 queen activity. The board and replay show Qd3 permits ...Rd8 and later exchanges, but the text does not isolate a forced tactical loss or necessary tactical resource.
findings.required_correction_or_limit: Retain coordination/activity as a moderate descriptive tag. Remove tactical calculation from the conservative tally unless a specific verified threat or exchange dependency is supplied. A legal PV and a large margin alone do not establish the tactical category.

findings.finding: h3 attacks the bishop on g4 before Nxc5. This is a concrete tempo and exchange-order contrast, not evidence that pawn structure is the issue.
findings.required_correction_or_limit: Remove pawn structures/breaks from the conservative tally. Retain tactical calculation only in its descriptive move-order sense: h3 Be6 Nxc5 Bxc4 Qa4. No mechanism claim follows.

findings.finding: After h6 the tested line allows ...Nxf5 and ...Nxh4+, whereas Ng3 protects f5 and h5 and supports king activity. The old phrase handles the pawn structure does not state this interaction.
findings.required_correction_or_limit: Replace pawn structures/breaks with coordination/activity; retain endgame decisions. Use the concrete knight coverage and opposing captures as rationale. The ending phase alone is not the evidence.

findings.finding: The alternative Ng5 moves an already-developed f3 knight. Be3 develops the c1 bishop; the alternative line instead brings both knights toward g5/b5 and c7.
findings.required_correction_or_limit: Retain coordination/activity. Remove opening/development from a conservative defect tally unless the category explicitly includes opening move choice without implying inadequate development. Do not infer delayed development from the phase label.

findings.finding: The rationale says after the reference concession, but its supplied selected anchors omit the immediately preceding reference root p22. The native board verifies ...Bh3 as a legal local resource, not that the previous reference move created it.
findings.required_correction_or_limit: Remove after the reference concession unless bound earlier/alternative evidence establishes it. Retain the local resource description. Separate opportunity response meaning a missed available resource from a confirmed opponent-created opportunity.

findings.finding: Rb7+ gains checking activity before the rook reaches d7 and captures d5. The played h4 line also captures d5, but with different timing and pawn placement. A pawn move by itself does not establish a pawn-structure failure.
findings.required_correction_or_limit: Retain endgame decisions and the concrete checking/timing description. Remove pawn structures/breaks from the conservative tally unless the h-pawn placement consequence is shown. The tactical tag is a descriptive forcing sequence, not proven search failure.

findings.finding: A tags three immediate-promotion resources as advantage preservation/conversion and explicitly denies a newly certified favorable episode. B uses primary to mean absence of a secondary tag. Neither establishes a primary loss cause or a complete favorable episode.
findings.required_correction_or_limit: Keep promotion-choice support and its three-root motif, but do not count three failed conversion episodes or a certified favorable episode. Rename primary counts nonsecondary-tagged. A missing historical secondary tag must remain unknown, not false.

findings.finding: A often uses opportunity response for any concrete missed resource; B uses it sparingly and at least once ties it to a reference concession. These are different category scopes.
findings.required_correction_or_limit: Use available concrete resource as a behavioral tag only with exact rationale. Add a separate opponent-created boolean with supported/unknown evidence, never infer it from adjacency. Do not aggregate current opportunity counts as a common rate before this distinction.

findings.finding: The challenger authored A. This is an independent review of B and a self-consistency review of A, not an independent challenge of both packets.
findings.required_correction_or_limit: A still needs a fresh reviewer for the final independent challenge. Both packets also need common-rule sampling before category-based priorities. Existing source numerical support is unaffected.

board_samples.rationale_before: Queen placement misses the active queen route before the central exchanges. The matched alternative starts Qb3 e4 Nxe4 Rb8 a4 Be6. This is a finite comparison, not a forced continuation.
The pawn challenge to the bishop is preferable before the knight capture. The matched alternative starts h3 Be6 Nxc5 Bxc4 Qa4 b5. This is a finite comparison, not a forced continuation.
Knight regrouping handles the pawn structure before the h-pawn advance. The matched alternative starts Ng3 Bf8 Kg4 Bh6 Ba3 Kd5. This is a finite comparison, not a forced continuation.
The knight route creates active squares before the bishop development. The matched alternative starts Ng5 Qe8 Nb5 h6 Nf3 Qe7. This is a finite comparison, not a forced continuation.
The bishop attack on h3 is a concrete missed resource after the reference concession. The matched alternative starts Bh3 Nd3 Rd8 Rc1 Bxg2 Kxg2. This is a finite comparison, not a forced continuation.
Rook checks and capture of the central pawn precede the flank pawn push. The matched alternative starts Rb7+ Kxa5 Rg7 d5 Rd7 Kb6. This is a finite comparison, not a forced continuation.

verdict: Numerical event identity and legal-line checks pass. Category totals are provisional pending explicit harmonization; do not rank from current cross-packet rates.

existing_boundary_case.issue: Existing seven-case list includes a floating-point lower edge at exactly .05 on the recorded decimal WDL grid. With the later-ledger 1e-9 tolerance this is not a strict straddler.
existing_boundary_case.disposition: Keep this as a separate boundary-convention sensitivity case with original unresolved status; do not promote it or remove its history. The 20 recomputed strict straddlers plus this boundary case yield 21 retained sensitivity records after adding 14 missing rows.
